title: Heat Pumps' 70% Savings Claim Is Real — Just Not For Your Bill
summary: UK explainer says the 70% heat pump saving is measured against resistance heating; against gas bills the saving is far smaller and depends on flow temperature and installation quality.

assertions.quote: the actual saving on your bill, once you switch from gas, lands closer to 20 to 30%, not 70%
genuinely uses about a third of the electricity to produce the same heat as a resistance heater
Because you're moving heat rather than creating it, one unit of electricity in can deliver three or more units of heat out
Manufacturer claims of 4.0 to 5.0 are lab numbers, not a British winter.

verdicts.note: Field trials (e.g. UK EoH, US monitoring) usually measure seasonal COPs below rated values, though good installs approach them.
Installed furnace efficiencies ran below rating, but the heat pumps' rated COPs at 17F were within the measurement error of the field data at all sites; small sample.
Steady-state COPs at 7 of 12 sites matched manufacturer values while the other 5 were lower, and measured capacity aligned with maximum rated capacity at only 5 of 12 sites.

Directly metered seasonal efficiencies of 152 mini-splits fell below their rated values on average, though some units met or exceeded their ratings; the evaluators blame usage patterns and test conditions, not misrated equipment.

Metering 160 heat pumps in 78 Maine homes over winter 2024-25, the field COP at each outdoor temperature fell between the manufacturers' AHRI COPs at maximum and minimum capacity, and was higher than earlier Maine studies of units installed 2014 to 2021; newer units roughly meet their ratings while older field results ran lower (one cold state, sample drawn from the lower two-thirds of users).

assertions.quote: a heat pump dropped into a house with the old gas boilers small radiators often disappoints
it's a mismatched installation being asked to do a harder job than it's suited for
Better insulation comes first because it helps regardless of what you end up choosing
gas per unit of energy is significantly cheaper than electricity in the UK
